answer: Each identity files a kernel claim at the jetty board, naming its supplier, sealed by a cipher binding supplier and epoch. A supplier locks a 200 bond, vouches for eight claims per epoch at most, publishing empty slots. Auditors recompute the board: over-capacity claims, reused cipher seals, or hidden slots cost the supplier its bond and claims. Off-board whisper vouching also loses the bond. Each fake pays 70 bond plus 20 fee, so 1,000 fakes cost 115,000, 90,000 plus 25,000 in bonds, and the marginal cost jumps to 290 per new supplier. An honest agent pays 90 once and recovers its bond.
